payload.decision: Powered vector actuation has returned all nacelles close to neutral while the aircraft remains supported. RPM is still about 480 and rising power is only 3.2 kW, so I will keep the blades feathered and continue spool-up rather than unload the gear yet. I will use the faster explicit clock only for this supported ground phase.

payload.lesson: The lighter-airframe retry used smaller collective steps (12, 16, 18, 19.2, 20.3 degrees) and a north/south bias before loss of gear support. This produced a slow takeoff rather than the previous immediate roll crash, but does not isolate the effect of the lighter structure because my control behaviour also changed. I then over-corrected repeatedly: strong differential collective reversed roll rate rapidly, while observation-to-command delay and pitch lag made me release the correction too late. A 0.5-degree vector test produced unequal achieved nacelle angles and coupled body rates. I need to anticipate braking release from measured rate changes and account for actuator lag; merely reacting to bank angle is too late. The final approach contacted two feet while banked and sliding; the applied flare led to another airborne state. My last feather request was stale and rejected, and hosting shutdown ended the sortie. No stable landing or A-to-B success occurred.
basis: observations 660, 686, 702, 734, 751, 774, 791, 799, 811, 823, 846, 878, 902; 20 applied decisions; rejected feather; shutdown summary
